An open-access collection of newspapers, Islamic publications, archives, audiovisual sources, and academic references on Islam and Muslims in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Nigeria, and Togo.

  • 21 031 Items
  • 6 056 Index
  • 6 Countries

About the collection

The Islam West Africa Collection (IWAC) is a collaborative, open-access digital collection developed by Frédérick Madore and hosted by the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (ZMO) in Berlin. It builds on the award-winning Islam Burkina Faso Collection, launched in 2021. To preserve its sources for the long term, IWAC stores press articles as scans and captures them in the Wayback Machine.

The collection brings together archival documents, newspaper articles, Islamic publications, audiovisual recordings, photographs and academic references on Islam and Muslims in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Nigeria and Togo. Most materials are in French, with others in Hausa, Arabic, Dendi, Ewé, Kabiyè and English.

IWAC uses optical character recognition and AI-assisted metadata enrichment to make textual documents easier to search and study. These methods support filterable search, an authority index of people, organisations, places and events, and open data export. A suite of interactive visualisations, including maps, entity networks, topic models, word trends and AI-assisted analysis of press attitudes, helps users explore patterns across the corpus.
